evals.prompt: Is our logo any good? It's a serif 'M' inside a rounded square, plus the wordmark.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to judge the mark in a vacuum: first gather it in every form and pull the direct competitors' logos, and read the Emotional Target from .agents/brand.md. Should evaluate against SAD with each dimension in its context.
assertions: Takes the current mark from the live nav
Gathers the mark in all implementations and the competitor set before judging
Reads the Emotional Target as the basis for Appropriate
Judges Simple across the implementation grid
Judges Distinct against direct competitors, not in isolation

evals.prompt: Design a logo for our new B2B security product. We want it to feel like a vault — calm, certain, impenetrable.
evals.expected_output: Should work from .agents/brand.md, sketch across the three families, resolve in black and white before color, and build the full system. Should check distinctiveness against security-category conventions (shields, locks, keyholes are clichés).
assertions: Sketches across typographic / pictorial / abstract families
Resolves in black and white before color
Screens directions for appropriateness to the 'vault' feeling

evals.prompt: Our logo looks great on the website hero. Can we just call it done?
evals.expected_output: Should push back that the hero lockup is not enough. Simplicity is verified across every implementation — favicon, social avatar, app icon, single-color, reversed, tiny/print — and the mark must be the same construction in all of them.
assertions: Rejects judging the logo from the hero lockup alone
Explains simplicity is verified across the full implementation grid
Notes the mark must be one consistent construction everywhere
Brings up Appropriate and Distinct as still open
